indicators.note: the island-and-people pair sits in the middle of the word for a specialist

parts.note: an expert is a specialist
men means people in general

explanation.surface: Islanders take part in a test run by an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the island-and-people pair after the fifth letter of the word for a specialist.
explanation.definitionFit: An experiment is a scientific test, a trial run to see what happens.

indicators.note: distraught means badly upset, so the letters of these three words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A young man is beside himself because his romance has gone wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: El Salvador is a nation of Central America.

parts.note: PE, physical education, is training of the body

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is working out in a practice zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is the pea plant, which climbs with tendrils.
explanation.definitionFit: The pea plant is a climbing vine that clings to supports with tendrils.

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
a part is a bit of something

explanation.surface: A ram took a bite out of something, and the castle's defenders are being asked about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: the rampart is where the castle's defenders stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampart is the broad defensive wall of a fort, where soldiers stood to fight off attackers.

clue.text: Prayer from crew on capsized craft

parts.note: to man a boat is to crew it

indicators.note: a capsized boat is upside down, so in this down clue the word is turned over

parts.note: art is a craft or skill

explanation.surface: Sailors pray after their boat overturns.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a sacred phrase chanted repeatedly in Hindu or Buddhist worship.

indicators.note: the hotel letter goes in the middle of the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A hotel stands in an agreeable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a comfortable or suitable role or place in life, a position that fits.

clue.text: Criminal covers same ground in cellar

indicators.note: one word covers another by wrapping round it

parts.note: bent is slang for corrupt or criminal

indicators.note: ground here is the past tense of grind, so the letters are milled into a new order

explanation.surface: A crook goes back over familiar territory down in a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a noun but is the past tense of grind, the anagram signal; 'covers' wraps the slang word for crooked around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A basement is the storey below ground level, much like a cellar.

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word for a shepherd

parts.note: warm means kind and caring

explanation.surface: A shepherd begins by looking after the sheep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flock' looks like sheep for the shepherd, but here it is a verb: to crowd together.
explanation.definitionFit: To swarm is to move in a dense crowd, just as people flock to a place.

clue.text: Divine drink within reach around court

indicators.note: around means the phrase for close by goes round the court letters

parts.note: near means close at hand, within reach

explanation.surface: The drink of the gods is close at hand, near the court.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth nectar was the drink of the gods, as ambrosia was their food.

clue.text: The PM arose to change prevailing mood

indicators.note: to change says the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister stood up to shift the national feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Atmosphere is the general feeling or tone of a place or occasion.

definitions.meaning: a limb, a member of the body
in cricket the ... side is also called the on side
a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A member of the cast is up on the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions. In cricket, a bat-and-ball game, the half of the field behind the batter's legs is both the leg side and the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg names a limb, the cricket side otherwise called on, and one stage of a journey.

parts.note: the saying 'between you, me and the' this object marks a secret shared by two people, so it is jokingly their shared confidant

explanation.walkthrough: The British saying 'between you and me and the gatepost' means 'in confidence', so the post is a third party privy to the secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatepost is the third party in a well-known phrase marking a confidential remark.

definitions.meaning: ... can mean consistency, as when two accounts are in ...

explanation.definitionFit: Agreement covers both accord between things, their consistency, and a binding deal between parties.

indicators.note: moved means the letters of the word are shifted into a different order

explanation.surface: A sensible person would relocate a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Astute means shrewd and perceptive, a near synonym of wise.

clue.text: Fuss about the French in Spanish city

indicators.note: about means the word for fuss goes round the French article

parts.note: a to-do is a fuss or commotion
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French visitors cause a commotion in a Spanish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famous for its steel.

clue.text: Lear's daughter in good heart leaves for season

indicators.note: the daughter's name sits in the middle of the two central letters
heart points to the central letters of the word good

parts.note: Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: One of King Lear's daughters is kind-hearted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'season' is a verb here, to add flavour, not a time of year; 'heart' and 'in' put the daughter between the two central letters of 'good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb whose leaves are used to flavour food.

clue.text: Graduate pens two articles in plant

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the graduate's letters go round the articles

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
an is the indefinite article, and two of them side by side give these letters

explanation.surface: A graduate writes a pair of pieces about a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' suggests a factory beside the writing graduate; it is the botanical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a large tropical plant as well as its fruit.

clue.text: Establishment no-one has a pop at

definitions.text: Establishment no-one has a pop at

parts.words: Establishment no-one has a pop at
parts.note: pop means father, so a home where no child has a dad; 'have a pop at' also suggests attacking

explanation.walkthrough: 'Have a pop at' is British slang for criticise, but pop is father: this is a home where no child has a father.
explanation.definitionFit: An orphanage is an institution caring for children who have lost their parents.

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as white as snow'
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: Something resembles a bird with grey plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashen means pale and grey like ash, as a frightened face looks.

indicators.note: in an across answer east is the right side, so reading from the east means right to left

parts.note: a pot is a vessel

explanation.surface: The first ship arrives out of the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Top means first or leading, as in top of the class.

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters of the word are twisted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A pupil grumbles that mathematics is hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricky' rearranges MATHS into STHMA. 'complaint' means an ailment here, not a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Asthma is a respiratory illness, and complaint is a common word for an ailment.

clue.text: Passage the writer will read aloud

indicators.note: read aloud means the answer sounds like the spoken contraction

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I, so 'the writer will' is I'll

explanation.surface: An author promises to give a reading of an extract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'read aloud' says the answer sounds like I'll; the setter calls themselves 'the writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passage.

indicators.note: seen in means the letters can be found inside these two words

explanation.surface: A runner is spotted on an Irish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' finds the letters straddling 'Lusk Island'. 'Runner' is not an athlete but something that slides.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long runner fixed to a boot for sliding over snow.

indicators.note: deviously means by a winding, crooked route, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is stirring up resentment by going behind one person's back.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to provoke their hostility or make them an enemy.
